mainEntity.name: Can composite bonding be repaired if it chips or breaks?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, yes. One of the advantages of composite bonding is that minor chips or fractures can often be repaired relatively easily by adding new composite material and reshaping the affected area. Whether repair is appropriate depends on the extent of the damage and the overall condition of the bonding. Your dentist will assess the bonded tooth and advise on the most suitable course of action. In some situations, replacing the bonding entirely may be recommended rather than patching it.

mainEntity.name: Does composite bonding stain over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin can absorb pigments from food and drinks over time, which may cause it to appear more yellow or discoloured compared to natural tooth enamel. This is a normal characteristic of the material. Regular professional polishing can help manage surface staining. Reducing the frequency of contact with heavily staining substances — such as coffee, red wine, and tobacco — can also help preserve the appearance of bonded teeth for longer.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding suitable for everyone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is a versatile treatment, but it is not appropriate for every patient or every clinical situation. Suitability depends on factors including the condition of the tooth, the patient's bite, the presence of any underlying dental issues, and the specific cosmetic goal being addressed. A thorough clinical examination is necessary to determine whether composite bonding is the right option or whether an alternative treatment may be more appropriate for your individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: How often should composite bonding be checked?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally advisable to have composite bonding reviewed at your regular dental check-up appointments, which for many patients are every six to twelve months. Your dentist can assess the condition of the bonding, check the surrounding gum tissue and tooth structure, and carry out professional polishing if needed. If you notice any changes between appointments — such as roughness, discolouration, or sensitivity — it is worth contacting your dental practice to arrange an earlier review.

mainEntity.name: Will composite bonding affect how I brush my teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding does not significantly change your oral hygiene routine, but some adjustments may help preserve the bonding. It is advisable to use a soft-bristled toothbrush and a non-abrasive fluoride toothpaste, as harsh abrasives can scratch the surface of the resin. Interdental cleaning remains important around bonded teeth to prevent plaque accumulation at the margins. Your dental hygienist can provide tailored advice on maintaining oral hygiene around bonded teeth.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding considered a long-term treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding is not considered a lifelong treatment. The material will naturally wear, stain, and age over time and will eventually require maintenance or replacement. This is a normal and expected part of the treatment's lifecycle. In many cases, bonding can be refreshed, repaired, or replaced without major intervention, which is one of the features that makes it a popular choice for patients seeking a less committal approach to cosmetic dentistry.
